clash_id: The clash's own id (C01, C02 ...); unique across the workbooks; playback_id: The orientation playback it is drawn in; event_id: The event (Events sheet) it belongs to: its dates, name and words come from there; kind: fight (a clash of arms) or capture (a post or stores taken with no fight recorded: drawn as a flag); won_by: The code of the side that won (Sides sheet), or indecisive. For a capture, the side that took it; result_method: stated (a cited source says who won) or inferred; result: The result in a few words, as the pane shows it; captured: What was taken: prisoners, guns, stores, the post; captured_by: The code of the side that took it; ships: The code of a side whose ships fought there: a small ship mark beside the symbol (Morgan, 25 Nov 2026: orientations only); disputed: yes if the sources disagree on the date or the result: the symbol carries a dagger and the pane gives both readings; other_won_by: The other reading: who it says won; other_reading: The other reading, in words; other_source_ids: The sources of the other reading; hypothesis_id: The Hypotheses row that records the disagreement (SR-19); place: Where it happened, in words; lat: Latitude of the symbol; lon: Longitude of the symbol; coord_source: How the place was found: marker, map_read, modern_map, derived, estimate; coord_precision_m: Good to about this many metres; coordinate_basis: How the place was found, in words; coordinate_confidence: high, medium or low; overall_confidence: high, medium or low (never high without a cited source: SR-21); source_ids: Sources for the result and the place (S01; S02)

cplace_id: The place's own id (CP01 ...); unique across the workbooks; playback_id: The orientation playback it is drawn in; name: Its name at the time; kind: city, town, village, fort, port, post or settlement; lat: Latitude; lon: Longitude; coord_source: How the place was found: marker, map_read, modern_map, derived, estimate; coord_precision_m: Good to about this many metres; coordinate_basis: How the place was found, in words; coordinate_confidence: high, medium or low; source_ids: Sources for the place

control_id: The row's own id (CT01 ...); unique across the workbooks; cplace_id: The place (Control places sheet); from: The date from which it is held this way (YYYY-MM-DD); held_by: The code of the side that holds it (Sides sheet), or contested (no side firmly holds it); basis: Why, in words: the capture, the evacuation, the treaty; event_id: The event that changed it, if there is one; method: stated (a cited source says who held it) or inferred; confidence: high, medium or low (never high without a cited source: SR-21); source_ids: Sources

One row per pair of playbacks that follow one another in a course chapter (for HIST 340: the South Carolina orientation, then Cowpens). The first one offers the next at its end, "Next in this chapter"; the next one offers the way back at the top of its side pane. Columns: link_id, from_playback and to_playback (playback ids from Playbacks, of this war), label and back_label (optional names), opens_at (optional: where the next one opens; its own opening view if empty), back_opens_at (optional: where the first one opens going back; its end if empty), chapter (the course chapter id), notes.
